    • Have gotten into Mac Miller again. I am listening to his posthumous albums for the first time (not Circles, I have always listened to and liked that one)
    • I am almost finished listening to Faces. I find it so fascinating what vibe the people who put it together have decided to curate to represent him - and of course what he represents of his own accord in the until-then-unreleased raps
    • Circles sounds like him speaking on death at the moment of death, right before and right after, as he lifts peacefully
    • Faces sounds almost like him talking about having been dead for 4 years or so, but from the voice of himself 4 years before death in some symmetrical verbage, with his death as the line of temporal symmetry
    • He is painted, in my eyes, as an amalgamation of many different lives, seen through the eyes of a careless trickster who dies again, and again, and again, throughout the album, but for who this continuously stopping-and-starting, fading-in-and-out existence is cause for interest, intrigue, celebration, or even mundanity
    • It feels fragmented by choice, rather than by happenstance. It of course would feel fragmented anyway, the album I’m assuming being many unreleased raps and unrelated half finished songs sewn together, but this fragmentation does not feel like it obstructs his voice.
    • Rather, it makes it obvious that the purpose of the album is NOT to even try to pretend to be his voice “as he would have spoken,” which is more similar to how Circles is. Instead, it seems clear that it is supposed to be a “omniscient third party” view, flickering in and out of non-chronological time at different disconnected parts of his life, purposely framed to be near nonsensical and alien and devilish yet familiar glimpses of his most far-reaching mental states
    • And almost carousel-esque, or circus-esque
    • While some of this is accomplished via what, again, I’m assuming are the purposeful artistic intentions of the group that posthumously put the album together, it is shocking how much also comes from his own voice. They obviously did a very good job taking disconnected phrases of Mac’s and, instead of trying to tie them together into one new overarching vision to make him say a larger thing he didn’t actually say, instead celebrate the incidental interconnectedness of each piece/verse and lean into the near drug/psychosis/psychedelic flickering of emotion and action that is what is left of the disparate recordings of him
    • The album does not feel like it came from him, but rather is an homage to him, which honestly I respect a lot
    • The “quality” of the songs is not what he himself would have put out, but the album makes it obvious that that’s not the point, and in doing so, I am able to really appreciate some of the songs as though from a “different artist,” where that artist is an impartial ghostly view of a period of lawlessness and death in his own mind, jesteringly yet artfully articulated as though by a puppet through his own past words

• A large part of social insecurity (in relation to how important you perceive yourself to be to others) or lack thereof is really reliant on how much you realize that moving past things doesn’t mean forgetting them, and doesn’t mean they no longer mean anything to you
    • I think a key thing I realized recently that “matured me” was the implicit understanding that the things in my life remain just as meaningful to me even when I am not engaged in them
    • Two things are understood at the same time. Things in your past are now there forever and cannot be brought to the present, they are forever done, time has moved on as it always does. At the same time, that doesn’t mean that their meaning is locked in the past. People I don’t talk to anymore still mean just as much to me as they did before. The addition of other things to my life - the fact that I have met other people, have looked elsewhere, have more and more and still continuously more experiences added on to my awareness - does not mean that they do not exist anymore. Coexistence alongside another thing in my mind does not devalue either one of them.
    • The paraphrase a quote from a movie lol (Her), the mind and heart are not boxes that get filled up; they grow and get bigger as they intake more things.
    • Me loving someone else does not mean I have any less love for people in the past
    • Me devoting myself to something new does not mean all my time devoting myself to something in the past was meaningless
    • I have recently been struck by this quote someone said; when asked “if you could have retroactively put 6,000 hour into anything, what would you put it into?” they essentially said “I would put it into [competitive game B] instead of [competitive game A]”, which has always struck me as a really small minded thing to say, but in writing this did I only really concretely realize why
    • There is backstory to this I suppose, but TLDR a competitive game is a competitive game is a competitive game, they can all be compared to one another insofar as they are closed systems where you try to be better than someone else at that closed system, using its rules and operating within it’s confines
    • So, that answer essentially means they wouldn’t put the 6000 hours into anything different or more meaningful; they are not only content to have all those hours be put into a closed system (which, unless you’re “going pro”, really outlives what it will teach you about life well before 6000 hours), but also that they don’t recognize that closed systems can all be compared to each other, and ALSO that they are so narrow minded in their scope of life and time that they only view competitive game B as “more relevant now” because they play it now. It shows that they think that because they stopped playing competitive game A, their time in it is now worthless, which really just highlights that they’re not playing EITHER competitive game as a conduit to actually learn more about themselves/life/etc, but rather as a TIME FILLER
    • And, yea this is a tangent from my original point I suppose, but I have become more and more against spending your life on time fillers instead of things that actively bring you meaning or fulfillment
    • IN SHORT, their answer showed that they DON’T understand my original point because they DON’T understand the continuing and prolonged important of past events on our current lives
    • I bring up a distinction now in my use of the word “past” events and experiences
    • Technically I mean this quite literally, but colloquially I should explain that by “past” I mean anything not happening RIGHT NOW
    • Why is this important?? Because a lot of the “things” or “events” that happen in our lives are not a single point in time, and can instead be understood as eras that we go though. I’m going to start using that word a lot lol
    • I’ll just give a bunch of examples instead of explaining this. The entirety of the time during which you know someone (i.e. four years) is the era of time you spent with them. The last three months you spent with them are their own era within that era. The entirety of the second year you knew them, starting nd ending in the past, is its own era. The time since I started drawing is an era. The time I drew since starting estrogen is an era. Starting estrogen is its own era outside of the context of drawing, yet still includes it. They time you ate a bunch of chicken for a few weeks is its own era. The time you started eating a sandwich last night to when you stopped eating a sandwich last night is it’s own era. That period of heavy stomached guilt you felt a few months ago is its own era.
    • Basically what I’m saying is that your relation to things is spread out over a long time, and you are not ENTIRELY 100% ENNGAGED WITH THE THING for the duration of that era
    • i.e. I was alone or with other people for PLENTY of time during “the era I knew that one person”
    • I was paying attention to something else, or drinking water or some shit, for a lot of the time during “the era I was eating that sandwich last night”
    • I had plenty of periods of contentedness or happiness during “that era of blackpitch guilt”
    • What does this mean? Essentially it just means that RIGHT NOW we are in COUNTLESS era that all overlap, influence each other, phase in and out of our awareness and attention, etc. I am not thinking of the fact that I’ve been having crazy dreams right before I wake up every morning for the past week when I am driving somewhere, but that doesn’t mean that it’s not something “currently happening to me” even dispite the fact that it is not literally “happening to me right now”
    • I’m gonna leave it there, because I think you see this gets into a really really nuanced subject of how arbitrary the things we group together are and how there are no real definite borders on anything, which is a topic I have invested a lot of myself into and love talking about, but nevertheless is not the core point i am trying to make here, so I’m going to leave that all as that for now
    • The tldr essential point is that a LOT of “threads” are all running concurrently in our lives even if they are not all active at once
    • A rephrasing for people who hated how cs-oriented that metaphor was; we are going through a lot of different shit in our lives at once even if, at any moment, we are only actively engaged in a small number of them
    • The point of me bringing this up is that, going back to what I started a lot of bullet points ago, something happening “in the past” is synonymous for my purposes here with “something you are currently going through, but which is not occupying your mind or senses right now”
    • Which, in turn, I will bring back to my original original original point. I had said that things that happen to us in the past do not lose mening even as they fall further behind and we accumulate more experiences. So too does this apply to the concept I was just talking about; things not currently in our focus do not lose their meaning to us just because we are not focused on them. Re-engaging with something brings back all of our feelings and emotions and experiences with that thing, even when we weren’t actively thinking about or even aware of those emotions and experiences when we were focused on something else
    • (Side note: I LOVE the phenomenon I just described and would love to make art about it, which I think was the point of my “sleep” video in a sense, but also extends past it. I find it fascinating that our emotions to something “exist to us” only “within us”, which (if you try following logic) means they phase the fuck out of existence when we don’t focus on them and spontaneously pop back up when we refocus on the things and remember the emotions. On second thought, I think the whole long bullet point train this side note sits inside of is actually just a long winded explaination of this very concept. Lol go figure. If you understand this side note and it’s ramifications feel free to stop reading this bc it’s essentially all just an expansion of this idea)
    • In short, from this, we can fully understand thatjust because we are not currently focused or engaged with a person we love does not mean we stop loving that person. Just because I am not currently drawing does not mean that I don’t love drawing. Just because I’m not currently eating tar does not mean I don’t want to eat tar
    • Which, once this is realized fully, comes with an understanding of a second reverse thing; just because I don’t love something doesn’t mean I can’t immerse myself fully in it, or in different words, doing something does not mean that that something “means the world” to me, or endures as a reflection of “who I am” forever
    • This, in turn, has different ramifications in different situations. Just because I never knit does not mean that I can’t be fully, actively, and truly engaged in a knitting class I decide to go to as a onetime thing. And, just because I was pathetic once does not mean I am a pathetic person.
    • I do drugs AND paint! I have passed out drunk at parties AND I will spend an hour looking at twigs! I have unfairly ignored or transgressed upon someone out of petty anger AND I have given parts of myself I didn’t need to give to people who “didn’t deserve it” because I wanted to help them!
    • Things in your life are transient, which both detaches you from them and also means that they will forever mean exactly what they mean to you (where that meaning can change and morph over time, but does not ‘diminish’, barring of course simple forgetfulness or old age, and yet even still I would argue they still mean just as much to you but simply will not affect you again)
    • From this, we arrive at the ultimate point that when empathy is introduced to this, we realize that this hold true for every single other person in the world at the same time. Luckily this realization often comes hand in hand with empathy just because of how maturity works
    • Other people also find things from the past, or things they aren’t focused on, meaningful to them
    • Which means that YOU, or the many many versions of you that exist to other people, remain just as important or meaningful to them even when you are not present with them, or are “currently making a bad impression on them”, etc
    • This is where this relates back to the ORIGINAL point on insecurity; it becomes way easier to NOT be insecure about yourself when you realize all of this, for reasons that are obvious if you understand this rant and which will hopefully be made clear to you at some point soon if you haven’t understood this rant

• I feel I am missing some link of understanding of myself between the following:
    • 1 - The fact that when I “become good at how I function”, I will seem simple and obvious and stupid (future note: this is just an extension/effect of 3, or vice versa)

    • 3 - I am reactive and experiential (look further into this one in general anyway)
    • I feel that when I do what I do well, it seems I am doing nothing. Like that quote that says when something is done really well, you don’t notice anything being done at all
    • Which I think ties into the reactive and experiential thing
    • Like, I consider myself really good at driving and making it a smooth experience because I read the road well and adjust seamlessly to have a nice ride, but because of that it just seems like I’m doing nothing at all. The ride is so seamless that passengers don’t notice that I DIDN’T hit that nastily spaced trio of potholes, and therefore don’t notice how tightly I squeezed between them - because the ride “stayed smooth” they assume nothing happened at all
    • I think I am able to extend the feeling of something so naturally that it seems it was just “a really potent feeling” that I happened to be there for rather than “something I did”
    • If you can’t tell there even was an extension or refining of the original thing, or at least you can’t tell “where it starts”, then it seems there WAS no extension or refining at all, and instead it seems like the original thing was just that good
    • As though my work fits so seamlessly into the original thing that it was the original thing’s doing instead of my doing
    • It is only really noticed when you look and realize that the heights to which the emotion or feeling or experience reached are too curated to be natural that you suddenly realize how much I did
    • Experiential → I let the experience do the talking because I have no desire to say anything myself, I figure if you have the same heightened experience that I did (or FELT I did) then you will understand the thing I would have wanted to say innately. This means that, when done well, it seems everything “the audience” “got” was from the experience rather than from me
    • Reactive → I build off of what emotion is there and where it is going. I don’t create something from nothing, I instead just “attune myself” to what emotion or experience is naturally emerging, then crystallize and heighten the effect of that experience.
    • Where active is more “playing off the crowd” and bringing people to your vision, reactive is more “playing off the experience” and bringing the vision to where the people are
    • Which is where the tricky thing that [name] touched on comes in, where at a deeper level “active” is actually reactive because it requires continually reading the audience to adjust trajectory, and “reactive” is actually active because it is a straight growth of the thing that becomes solid enough to reach people regardless of trajectory or (”mental”) placement
    • And I think perhaps I know why this in turn makes me intimidating
    • A) it seems that I don’t care for where you are and B) I reach you anyway
    • When I know what I’m about, I think the effect is that I simply give off powerful waves of emotion or assuredness despite seeming like I’m not doing much. Almost like, pardon the phrasing, a well adjusted emotional version of the archetype of the small-and-unassuming fighter that nevertheless has an inexplicable deadly aura (DBZ SPOILERS) like final from freiza or boo
    • It IS intimidating to interact with someone who seems so unassuming, who seems like they so poignantly DON’T have a goal they are trying to reach in the conversation, who seems so content, yet who obviously “knows what they’re about” and for lack of better phrasing “maintains a strong aura” despite seeming like they couldn’t care less about their aura, as though their naïvete and simple childlike eagerness belies, or even comes from, the fact that they don’t feel the least bit threatened or compulsed to try and manipulate the conversation
    • (Note: “couldn’t care less about their aura” not from nonchalance or anything, but due to the fact that they seem to be okay with making a fool out of themselves or abruptly being really vilnerable without thought if how it would reflect on them)
    • It makes a less secure person feel strange for “overcompensating” in an interaction that seems, from the other party, to be so almost-painfully simple and of-utmost-importance-via-being-absolutely-inconsequential
    • And because of this, or alongside this, that makes it that much more impactful when I manage to exercise my artful little power of “reaching you” with some emotion or experience

• My background anxiety has morphed into background clutter
    • I meditated today for the first time in a little bit. It took several tries, and a long time of sitting, before my mind quieted into a familiar state of silence and openness
    • It felt like there was just so much running in the background of my mind. This makes sense, since I have been very busy/occupied lately and have not “sat and done nothing” much recently
    • This obviously causes things to bubble up in my mind, spill over, run and run and run as I live my life
    • I’ve gone over this before, but I suppose I’ll say it anyway
    • The mind needs time where it isn’t continuously being input new experiences or sensations so that it can mull over what it has experienced recently
    • It is hard to properly process or think about the things you experience if you are constantly experiencing. Your mind naturally stays on the frontier of sensation it is experiencing, so if said frontier is always popping, your mind will always be there
    • As such, a backlog of unexamined experiences and memories will start to form
    • I think “best practice” is to give yourself time daily to let this backlog take the center stage of your mind in a messy and faded jumble of thoughts and musings. Not as a directed thing, i.e. not sitting down and systematically going back through the day or whatever, but literally just letting your mind sit in silence for a moment.
    • If it’s given nothing, this backlog will naturally well up, where your brain begins to pick at it and sift through it, making connecting and picking out interesting bits you caught but didn’t fully pay attention to when they happened. Events phase in and out of the front of your mind in an unordered heap, and this is good - this is exactly what I want, as I experience the most potent retroflection this way (yucky phrasing)
    • If you don’t give your mind time to do this for an extended period of time, the backlog starts to get unhandleable, and when you finally give your mind time for silence, the backlog will rush through like a tsunami. This is what I experienced today. Things crash through your mind, thought circles run and run, the legs of your mind pitter and patter and pitter and patter, running from this subject to that, trying to finish this thought line or that one, trying to figure this out or that in a jumble that sure FEELS productive, but also is just kind of frazzled and rushed and frenzied
    • You will be surprised how many things pop up, how many different things your mind has remembered and been struck by, when you finally allow for external silence. Idea after idea after idea after idea, subject after subject after subject after subject. The TV show I watched recently, an album I saw but didn’t listen to, the artist of that album’s other works, music I have listened to recently, music my friend has made, my relationship with music, etc etc etc - all in the span of just 10 or 20 minutes, in between slices and slices and slices of other topics
    • It is not that the mock train of thought I just described is BAD - indeed, I have had similar trains of thought when I routinely give my mind ample time to reflect. It is that, when your mind doesn’t have much free time, the train of thought feels compulsive - even if you WANT to silence yourself, you mind simply CAN’T
    • Having a difficult time silencing your mind during this isn’t really an issue, past the time spent letting your mind tire itself out.
